_note: Structure Arc slice 1 (STRUCTURE-ARC-LOCKS-2026-08-05.md LOCK 1/2/3) — the recovered manual's fixed questline. Five Operations, identical in every generated world, one per procedurally-placed dungeon site (worldgen.js DUNGEON_SITE_COUNT=5). `dungeonSlot` indexes the world's dungeon sites sorted nearest-to-farthest from spawn (src/engine/manual.js orderDungeonSites) — that ordering is what assigns MEANING onto already-procedural positions; it never touches placement itself (LOCK 2's placement fork stays resolved to (b)). Operation 5 is always the farthest dungeon and is therefore 'the Chapel' (LOCK 3) — src/engine/manual.js's isChapelSite() is the single source of truth for this, replacing the old id/name regex guess that only worked when a site's randomly-templated name happened to say 'Chapel'. `teaches` is factual/mechanical (which real, already-shipped system the operation walks the player through) and is NOT a naming item. `title`/`gates`/`pointerHint`/`intro` were authored by WEISS 2026-08-05 night (Ray routed CHP voice calls to Weiss this session; Weiss calibration: DRAFT-ONLY band). RAY BLESSED THE FULL SET 2026-08-06 (titles, gates, pointers, intro beats, op1 relic) — this is operator-approved voice; edits are his to make, not a pending gate. `gates` is DESCRIPTIVE (which capability the operation's completion narratively represents becoming legible/available) — completing an operation does NOT mechanically lock/unlock any verb; the world stays open and every site is enterable in any order, exactly as shipped. `status` (locked/active/complete) is the MANUAL's own display bookkeeping only. `completion.type: clearSite` reads the EXISTING session.clearedSites() signal — session.clearSite(site.id) already fires the moment any fight is won inside a dungeon (src/main.js combat-return handling) — no new completion mechanic was added.
introBeats: You found the manual. It was left on a bench with no name on the cover.
The manual contains five operations. They are printed in sequence and do not change.
Whoever runs the operations becomes the thing people whisper about. The pattern follows them regardless.

operations.title: Baseline Survey
operations.teaches: first-person dungeon crawling (forward/back, turning) and the four-verb tactical combat loop (strike/guard/reach/gambit) against a mundane single foe, in a hand-authored layout
operations.pointerHint: Proceed to the nearest service tunnel and note that the walls are already dry.

operations.title: Entity Assessment
operations.teaches: reading a being before you fight it — sneaking past a visible dungeon enemy (NERVE-gated) or opening a parley (the stat-gated approach verbs) instead of striking
operations.gates: How to read what watches back
operations.pointerHint: Follow the drainage line to the secondary shaft where the air moves against the wind.

operations.title: Transit Authorization
operations.teaches: the work of passage — world gates that stay shut until a tagged traversal item is spent at them, found as loot in the biomes that border a gate
operations.pointerHint: Cross to the third junction and find the gate; it opens only when the ledger matches.

operations.title: Ledger Reconciliation
operations.teaches: the record keeps its own account — the journal's corruption and ghost entries rising with hidden exposure (FNORD), so what you wrote and what you read start to differ
operations.gates: The ledger keeps its own count
operations.pointerHint: Travel past the municipal boundary to the railyard and observe that the tracks do not connect.

operations.title: Terminal Audit
operations.teaches: the Chapel — full-register collision (every register speaks over the others at once) and the far harder 'chapel' encounter table; the rumored entity's theory resolves here, unconfirmed either way
operations.pointerHint: Continue to the end of the grid where the pavement stops; the structure waits without a door.
